_comment: The specification freeze. This file is the mechanical form of one rule:
DO NOT MODIFY THE SPECIFICATION TO MAKE THE MEASUREMENT APPARATUS PASS.
An implementation or a measurement system disagreeing with SEMANTICS.md is
evidence to investigate, never grounds to edit the specification. If the
specification genuinely needs to change, that change must be recorded here
as an explicit semantic decision, with a rationale, and it must carry a
version bump. Silent drift is what converts the loop
into a closed optimisation loop in which the system converges by optimising
`spec_freeze.py` verifies these digests. If any pinned file changes without
a recorded decision here, verification FAILS and names the file.

decisions.rationale: Initial ratified semantics: grounded consequence, cyclic defeat unresolved, three uncertainties kept distinct.

Independent implementation B disagreed on five cases for one reason: A enforced five corpus-integrity invariants present in NEITHER public document. This is a SPECIFICATION FAILURE, not an implementation defect. Added chapters 2.1 (INVALID carries CORPUS), 4.6 (absent values have no implied meaning), 5a (proposition-level selection separated from grounding), and defined represented_reason. Evidence: deleg_ade63b6a, MILESTONE-SIT-V0.1.md.

Family H exposed three gaps, none of which was an implementation defect. (1) F-1: an exhausted iteration budget was reported as SEMANTIC, converting an operational limit into an epistemic claim. (2) DEFEATED was advertised as a capability but no valid corpus case could reach it end to end; it was reserved rather than implemented, because fabricating an invalid fixture to reach it would have been CORPUS FAILURE. (3) REFUSED uncertainty and INVALID-over-REFUSED precedence were unstated. Added 6.1-6.4. Evidence: MILESTONE-SIT-V0.3.md, impl_d.

rule: A specification change requires a new version, a rationale naming the
semantic ambiguity or defect, and the evidence that surfaced it.
A specification change may NOT be motivated by an implementation or a
measurement system disagreeing with the specification. Disagreement is
evidence to investigate the implementation, or evidence that the
specification is silent, never grounds to edit it silently.
If an independent implementation is CORRECT and disagrees with the
specification, that is a specification gap and warrants a decision here.
If it is INCORRECT, that is an implementation defect and warrants nothing
here. Distinguishing the two requires reading the specification, not
The neutral corpus defines what observations were supposed to exist. The
implementations define what they derive. The comparator establishes whether
all of them were observed and compared. These are three questions and they
belong to three different parties; conflating them is MEASUREMENT FAILURE.
